The Apple Compote Affair

Within my pot of steaming dreams,
The apples dance their sweet ballet,
While cinnamon and sugar schemes
To sweep their tartness clean away.

Like rubies in a crystal crown,
The fruit descends in graceful swirls,
Each piece a dancer floating down
As steam above them gently twirls.

I watch them simmer, soft and slow,
These orchard gems from autumn's heart,
Till every apple learns to glow
And play its designated part.

My spoon conducts this fruity scene
With gentle strokes of practiced care,
Till every drop becomes serene—
A liquid jewel beyond compare.

At last, when evening dims the sky,
My patience yields its sweet reward:
A draft that makes the angels sigh,
A taste that kings would die toward.

So raise your glass of autumn gold,
Let memories of orchards shine—
This simple pleasure, ages old,
Makes every moment more divine.
